dedupe_keys.name: target2 outage of 23 october 2020 and the independent review of the 2020 target services incidents deloitte for the ecb

description: This case study covers the outage of TARGET2, the euro area's real-time gross settlement system, on 23 October 2020 and the independent review of it and four other 2020 incidents in the TARGET Services. On that day access to all TARGET2 applications was lost and settlement stopped for about eleven hours, delaying payments, ancillary system transactions and liquidity transfers to the T2S securities settlement and TIPS instant payment services. The root cause was a configuration parameter that triggered a software bug in the switches of the private network linking the four operating central banks; the vendor had known of the bug since May 2020, but it was not in the manuals or release notes. The review was carried out by Deloitte for the European Central Bank from December 2020 to March 2021 and published on 28 July 2021 as a free, partly redacted PDF, which readers access after accepting a hold harmless agreement. Coverage is the euro area payment infrastructure. It reports 40 findings, 17 of high severity, in change management, business continuity, fail-over and recovery testing, crisis communication, governance and data centre operations. Caveats: security-sensitive detail is redacted. For simulation it documents how a single network fault disabled both sites and cascaded across linked settlement services, a reference scenario for resilience and emergency response studies of financial infrastructure. It is related to the ECB TARGET2 liquidity stress test case study and the TARGET Services records in this catalogue.
